_comment: EXP-1215: the wording of every confirm/choice prompt, byte-identical on web (packages/ui Prompt), iOS (ExpUI GlassAlert), Android (ui/components/GlassAlert) and the desktop IDE (EXP-1230: domain prompts.rs, drawn in its native alert windows by AlertSpec::from_prompt, which maps the roles onto its buttons and focus onto Return). HOW CLIENTS USE IT: each client keeps ONE constants file that mirrors `prompts` (title, body, action labels, roles, order, focus) and one test that reads this fixture and compares every string; a prompt site renders an entry by id and fills the {placeholders} named in `params`, nothing else. A client that does not show a prompt simply has no site for it; a client that adds one later takes the entry as is. COPY RULES: the title is ONE question that names the object. Names a person typed for a thing (team, board, label, file, device, passkey) sit in straight double quotes; issue identifiers, people, repositories, servers and sign-in providers are unquoted. `body` exists only for a fact the title cannot carry (what else is deleted, a consequence for other people, where it can be restored, what is kept); no body key = no body line; never a restatement of the buttons, never 'Are you sure?'. Plain, literal, sentence case, no em dashes, no curly quotes. VERBS: Delete = permanent removal; Move to trash = restorable; Remove = detaching (member, repository, device, server, passkey, password); Unlink = a sign-in provider (the pair of its row's Link); Leave; Stop; Resume; Merge; Move. The answer's label is the title's verb alone ('Delete', 'Remove', 'Merge'), except where the verb alone says nothing ('Move to trash', 'Make owner', 'Make member'). A busy answer keeps its label (no 'Deleting...'); the pill's spinner shows the work. VARIANT KEYS: `titleOne`/`titleMany` and `bodyOne`/`bodyMany` where a {count} appears (One = exactly 1); any other `title<Case>`/`body<Case>` key is explained by the entry's `variants`. ACTIONS are in DISPLAY order, leading to trailing: a leading `quietDestructive` first if any, then the trailing pills left to right, the `default`/`primary` answer last. Roles: `cancel` = the plain pill that only dismisses (scrim tap, Esc and system back take the same path); `default` = a plain pill that does something; `primary` = the accent pill, the safe or expected answer; `destructive` = the plain pill with a destructive label and tinted border, the answer of a plain destructive confirm beside Cancel (such a prompt has NO primary); `quietDestructive` = destructive text with no fill or border, set apart on the leading edge, used only beside a safe primary. `focus` = the action id that takes initial focus and Enter/Return: the primary when there is one, the cancel action in a plain destructive confirm and in a consent (a host asking before a surface acts as the person: the answer is `default`, never `primary`, so Enter denies), never a destructive answer. A content-slot text field (web's type-the-name inputs) takes focus instead and Enter then does nothing until its answer is enabled. LAYOUT, the same on the three cards: ONE row of 32pt `md` pills at the bottom of the card; a leading quiet destructive answer sits apart on the leading edge, every other answer packs on the trailing edge in display order. When the row does not fit the card's width it STACKS: one natural-width pill per line, each aligned to the trailing edge, in REVERSE display order (the default/primary answer first, Cancel last, a quiet destructive answer last of all). No two-row hybrid (never some pills wrapped and some not), no full-width blocks, no solid red buttons. While an answer runs, its pill shows the pill's spinner and the whole row plus the dismiss paths (scrim, Esc, back) are disabled. LOCKED ELSEWHERE, not repeated here (these keep their own fixture or shared constant, and take only the roles, focus and layout rules above): issue-draft.json (discard confirm, leave prompt), blocked-start.json (start a blocked issue), stack-merge-choice.json (merge a stack member), close-pr.json (close PR without merging), the steer `/clear` confirm (contract steerCommands + steerCommandConfirmCopy / SlashCommands), the agent-account Remove and Sign out sentences (removeAccountConfirmCopy / removeAmbientAccountConfirmCopy / signOutConfirmCopy, AgentAccountsRows), the GitHub disconnect strings (GH_DISCONNECT_* / GithubCopy). Prompts that exist on ONE platform only (web settings, billing and admin) are not listed until a second client shows them. Bodies state only what holds on every team: what a merge does to issue statuses and live runs depends on the team's settings, so the merge prompts do not promise it, and stop-run has no body.

delete-issue.title: Delete {identifier}?
delete-issue.body: Its comments and files are deleted with it.

delete-issues.bodyOne: Its comments and files are deleted with it.
delete-issues.bodyMany: Their comments and files are deleted with them.

params.name: count
params.meaning: how many issues are selected in the list

delete-file.title: Delete "{filename}"?
delete-file.body: A description or comment that embeds it shows a deleted image note instead.

move-issue.title: Move {identifier} to "{board}"?
move-issue.body: It gets a new identifier in that board.

merge-issue-pr.title: Merge PR #{number}?
merge-issue-pr.bodyMany: It is squash-merged. It covers {count} issues.
merge-issue-pr.variants: titleNoNumber when the pull request number is not known yet. bodyOne when the pull request links one issue, bodyMany for a batch pull request.

params.name: count
params.meaning: how many issues the pull request links (2 or more)

merge-run-pr.title: Merge PR #{number}?
merge-run-pr.body: It is squash-merged. No issue is linked to it.
merge-run-pr.variants: titleNoNumber when the pull request number is not known yet.

params.name: number
params.meaning: the GitHub pull request number of a run's own, issue-less pull request

merge-external-pr.title: Merge {repository}#{number}?
merge-external-pr.body: It is squash-merged into {base}. No issue is linked to it.

params.name: number
params.meaning: the GitHub pull request number of an open pull request no issue or run links (EXP-1244, the Reviews repository bands)

resume-run.title: Resume this run on {device}?
resume-run.body: The agent continues where it stopped, in the same worktree.
resume-run.variants: titleNoDevice when the device that ran it has no known label.

params.name: device
params.meaning: the label of the device that ran the run, unquoted

delete-action.title: Delete "{name}"?
delete-action.body: Its triggers are deleted with it. Its runs stay and live ones keep going.

remove-device.title: Remove "{name}"?
remove-device.body: A device with the daemon still running registers again on its next heartbeat.

params.name: name
params.meaning: the device label, or the device id when it has none

delete-team.title: Delete "{name}"?
delete-team.body: All its boards, issues and files are deleted for good.
delete-team.slot: web: the type-the-team-name field (it takes focus; Delete stays disabled until the name matches).

trash-board.title: Move "{name}" to trash?
trash-board.body: After 48 hours it is deleted with all its issues. Until then an owner can restore it in team settings on the web.

delete-label.title: Delete "{name}"?
delete-label.body: It comes off every issue that has it.

params.name: name
params.meaning: the member's display name (their email when they have none)

leave-team.title: Leave "{name}"?
leave-team.body: You need a new invite to come back.

make-owner.title: Make {name} an owner?
make-owner.body: Owners can manage members and billing, delete boards and delete the team.

make-member.title: Make {name} a member?
make-member.body: They can no longer manage members or delete boards.

unlink-sign-in-method.title: Unlink {provider}?
unlink-sign-in-method.body: Your other sign-in methods keep working. You can link it again any time.

params.name: provider
params.meaning: the sign-in provider's name (Google, Apple, GitHub, an OIDC provider)

remove-password.title: Remove your password?
remove-password.body: Your other sign-in methods keep working.

remove-passkey.title: Remove the passkey "{name}"?
remove-passkey.body: The copy on your device stays until you delete it there.

params.name: name
params.meaning: the passkey's name, 'Passkey' when it has none

delete-account.title: Delete your account?
delete-account.body: Teams where you are the only member are deleted with all their issues. In shared teams your issues stay and your comments are deleted.
delete-account.variants: titleOnServer on the clients that can hold several servers (iOS, Android).
delete-account.slot: web: the consequences list (it adds the subscription facts, billing is web-only) and the type-your-email field (it takes focus; Delete stays disabled until the email matches). Web shows that list IN PLACE of `body`.

remove-server.title: Remove {server}?
remove-server.body: You are signed out and its data on this device is deleted. You can add it again any time.

exponential-ui-consent.title: Allow this surface to run {tool}?
exponential-ui-consent.body: It acts as you, with your access to this team.

params.name: tool
params.meaning: the MCP tool a harness.mcp call runs, else the host function's own name
